snp1.6:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
snp1.6:1.3: Then a certain god, towards the end of the night, whose surpassing beauty lit up the whole of Jeta’s Wood, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he stood on one side.
snp1.6:1.4: While standing on one side that god recited a verse to the Fortunate One:
snp1.6:2.2: regarding the man going to ruin -
snp1.6:2.3: we have come to ask the Fortunate One,
snp1.6:2.4: what is the cause of ruination?”
snp1.6:3.1: “The thriving man is easy to know,
snp1.6:3.2: the ruining man is easy to know,
snp1.6:3.3: the thriving man loves the Dhamma,
snp1.6:3.4: the ruining man hates the Dhamma.”
snp1.6:4.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:4.2: this is the first ruin (of man).
snp1.6:4.4: what is the second cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:5.2: he does not endear the good,
snp1.6:5.3: he is pleased with the Dhamma of the bad,
snp1.6:5.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:6.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:6.2: this is the second ruin (of man).
snp1.6:6.4: what is the third cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:7.1: “That man who is fond of sleep, fond of society,
snp1.6:7.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:8.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:8.2: this is the third ruin (of man).
snp1.6:8.4: what is the fourth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:9.1: “He who, when his mother or father has grown old,
snp1.6:9.3: though having much, does not support them,
snp1.6:9.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:10.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:10.2: this is the fourth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:10.4: what is the fifth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:11.1: ° “He who deceives a brahmin, or an ascetic,
snp1.6:11.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:12.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:12.2: this is the fifth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:12.4: what is the sixth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:13.2: who has gold, who has food,
snp1.6:13.3: but who eats his sweetmeats alone,
snp1.6:13.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:14.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:14.2: this is the sixth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:14.4: what is the seventh cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:15.1: “That man who is proud of his birth,
snp1.6:15.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:16.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:16.2: this is the seventh ruin (of man).
snp1.6:16.4: what is the eighth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:17.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:18.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:18.2: this is the eighth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:18.4: what is the ninth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:19.1: “(He who is) not satisfied with his own wives,
snp1.6:19.3: and is seen with other mens’ wives,
snp1.6:19.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:20.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:20.2: this is the ninth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:20.4: what is the tenth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:21.1: “A man who, being past his youth,
snp1.6:21.2: brings home a young girl (for his wife),
snp1.6:21.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:22.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:22.2: this is the tenth ruin (of man).
snp1.6:22.4: what is the eleventh cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:23.1: “A woman given to drink, a spendthrift,
snp1.6:23.2: or a man of similar sort,
snp1.6:23.4: that is a cause of ruination.”
snp1.6:24.1: “Indeed it is so, this we know,
snp1.6:24.2: this is the eleventh ruin (of man).
snp1.6:24.4: what is the twelfth cause of ruin?”
snp1.6:25.1: “One who is poor, but has great craving,
snp1.6:25.2: who is born in a family of nobles,
snp1.6:25.3: and who wants to be king,
snp1.6:25.4: that is a cause of ruination.
snp1.6:26.1: The wise man who reflects on (the cause of) these ruins
snp1.6:26.3: a noble one, endowed with insight,
